clue.text: Dissension ensued when fellow prepared a tonic

indicators.note: prepared means made up afresh, so the letters of a tonic are reworked

explanation.surface: A row broke out after a man mixed someone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges A TONIC into ACTION, which follows F.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group, and the word also means internal discord or strife.

clue.text: Solemn pledge from funeral directors

explanation.surface: Undertakers give a serious promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm undertaking is a binding promise; read the other way, an undertaking firm is a company of morticians.

clue.text: Cake, but not beefcake!

parts.note: the word is a teatime griddle cake and also British slang for attractive women, as opposed to beefcake meaning muscular men

explanation.surface: A teatime treat that is no hunk.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUMPET is a soft griddle cake eaten toasted in Britain, and dated slang for attractive women.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumpet is a small spongy cake, and slang for women regarded as sexually attractive.

clue.text: Popular man, they say, with sincere intentions

indicators.note: they say signals a word that sounds like the one we enter

parts.note: in means popular, and Ernest is a man's name

explanation.surface: A well-liked fellow is said to mean what he says.
explanation.walkthrough: IN plus ERNEST, said together, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in earnest is to be serious and sincere.

clue.text: Fancies renovating inns, too

indicators.note: renovating means rebuilding, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: Ideas about doing up pubs as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Notions are ideas or whims, like fancies.

clue.text: Got together and went discoing

explanation.surface: Some friends met up and spent the night at a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubbed together means pooled resources as a group; to go clubbing is to visit nightclubs.

clue.text: Cathedral canons read it from the bible

explanation.surface: Clergy read aloud a passage of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral's governing body of canons is its chapter; scripture is divided into numbered chapters.

clue.text: You sound prudent enough to get treatment

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is replaced by a letter pronounced the same

parts.note: you is pronounced like the letter U
sage means wise or prudent

explanation.surface: Being sensible is enough to earn good care.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is handled or treated.

clue.text: Term for spa of ill-repute

parts.note: Bad is the German word for a spa, as in Baden-Baden
a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A resort town with a poor reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD prefixes German spa towns such as Bad Ems.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad name is a poor reputation, being in disrepute.

clue.text: Wait to discover numbers at the hop

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
attendance is the number of people present

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about to find how many came to the party.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance attendance is to wait on someone obsequiously.

clue.text: A way to defeat enemies with energy

parts.note: to rout is to defeat a foe decisively
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A recipe for military victory: beat the enemy with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a road or path taken to a destination.

clue.text: Enraged at disturbance in dining area

indicators.note: a disturbance upsets the order of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper at a commotion in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor spot where refreshments are served.

clue.text: Principal stimulant taken by the majority

parts.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug
most means the greater part

explanation.surface: Most people are now taking a particular drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means foremost or chief, the top in importance.

clue.text: Escape from Geneva, despite police patrols

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of a run of the following words

explanation.surface: A fugitive gets out of the Swiss city though officers are on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across GenEVA DEspite; 'police patrols' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or elude pursuers.

clue.text: Hesitates to shred it differently

indicators.note: differently means the letters are arranged in another order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to tear a document up another way.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to waver indecisively.

clue.text: Turn tail, only to stand again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to stand someone a drink is to treat them

explanation.surface: A soldier flees, only to rally and hold position again.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'stand' a round is to treat someone, a British pub idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or flee from danger.

clue.text: Problem-solvers contemplate a reservoir

parts.note: to contemplate is to think
a tank is a container for liquid

explanation.surface: Engineers ponder a water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A think tank is a group of experts assembled to devise solutions.

clue.text: Told by one of one's kin

explanation.surface: A story recounted by a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means narrated, and also means connected by blood to a relative.

clue.text: Watchman needs to watch his back

explanation.surface: A sentry must guard against attack from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a sentry; to look out is to be careful of danger.

clue.text: Hesitating to ennoble someone indebted

parts.note: to dub is to confer a knighthood
a debtor issues IOUs, notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Reluctance to knight a man in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious means uncertain or doubtful about something.

clue.text: Dot wants a small drink

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Dorothy fancies a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to mark a surface with many small specks.

clue.text: Trumpeters going to main Welsh port

parts.note: the trumpeter is a species of swan
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: Birds fly off over the ocean from a harbour in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Trumpeters' is loose: one SWAN is needed, or read SWANS overlapping the S of SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city with docks in south Wales.

clue.text: Maybe he is supporting no-one in France

parts.note: pro means in favour of
taken as written
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who backs nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' shows 'he' is one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: He is an example of a word standing in for a noun.

clue.text: Unanimous about the time to lunch

explanation.surface: Everyone agreed it was nearly time to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at one is to be in agreement; one o'clock is a usual lunch hour.

clue.text: Presenter is English engineer in Maine

indicators.note: in places the engineer inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A TV host is an Englishman working in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies who hosts a show.

clue.text: Very dark-yellow oil

parts.note: black is the darkest shade
gold is a yellow colour

explanation.surface: An oil paint described by its deep ochre hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Black gold is a nickname for crude petroleum, prized like a precious metal.

clue.text: Military award makes press angry

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: A medal ceremony upsets the journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests journalists; it is the ironing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a German decoration for bravery.

clue.text: Trouble sailors on deck

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Seamen cause a disturbance on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like part of a ship; it is the verb to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, as in decking the halls.

clue.text: Ready-to-cook chicken?

parts.note: a bird prepared for the oven has had its innards removed, while a chicken is also a coward lacking courage

explanation.surface: A supermarket label for an oven-ready bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking guts means lacking courage, and a cleaned bird literally has no guts.

clue.text: Question an Anglican quizzically?

parts.note: to question is to ask
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Someone interrogates a clergyman with a puzzled look.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to regard with doubt or suspicion.
